subject: Follow-up: Security & compliance next steps — SOC 2 Type II, data residency, evidence handoff
body:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lim <sara.lim@hearthline.com>, Carlos Mendez <carlos@hearthline.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: Security & compliance next steps — SOC 2 Type II, data residency, evidence handoff

Hi Sara / Carlos —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we have alignment on timelines and owners: 

- Scope check: Hearthline is asking about SOC 2 Type II report availability (full period report covering infra + application layers). You mentioned payroll/data processing integrations and an EU data residency requirement for certain customer datasets.
- Ask list: SOC 2 Type II PDF (latest period), bridge letter (temporary attestation while report is in progress), vendor security questionnaire (DDQ), and evidence access for a short-lived secure bucket or SFTP.
- Timeline: You said procurement would prefer evidence access and the bridge letter within 7–10 business days if possible. Full report delivery is subject to auditor schedule; we'll confirm ETA.

Action items we propose (owner in parentheses):
1) Send SOC 2 Type II scan and provisional bridge letter draft (Aditya) — attach preliminary bridge letter draft for your review.
2) Kick off vendor DDQ — we can either complete the OneTrust questionnaire link you provide or send our DDQ spreadsheet (Lauren).
3) Provision a secure evidence handoff (SFTP or pre-authenticated object) and list of initial artifacts we plan to upload (Dylan).
4) Confirm data residency controls and any required contractual addenda (Aditya + Legal) — you mentioned GDPR + HIPAA concerns for EU-hosted datasets.

Attachments: redwood_evidence_checklist_v1.pdf (high-level list of commonly requested artifacts), sample_bridge_letter_draft.docx

If that matches your view, Sara — can you: 1) confirm the preferred mechanism for the DDQ (OneTrust vs our spreadsheet), 2) confirm the primary procurement contact for DocuSign/POs, and 3) confirm whether the EU data residency concern applies to all production data or a subset of customer PII?

Thanks — I’ll standby to share the bridge letter draft and push the evidence checklist.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0132

---

From: Sara Lim <sara.lim@hearthline.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Carlos Mendez <carlos@hearthline.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Security & compliance next steps — SOC 2 Type II, data residency, evidence handoff

Hi Aditya —

Thanks for the clear recap. That aligns with our notes. A few clarifications: 

- DDQ: we prefer to use OneTrust — I9ll send an invite to your security contact. The link is https://onetrust.example.com/forms/HEARTH-CCQ-2026.
- Report scope: SOC 2 Type II must include the processing and hosting layers for customer data; our legal team will want confirmation on third-party subprocessors.
- Data residency: this is a subset of customer PII tied to EU-based customers — not our entire environment. We9ll need to see controls around cross-region replication and encryption key location.
- Procurement: Carlos will be the DPO/corp procurement contact for contract routing and billing.

If you can get the bridge letter and a short artifact list over by EOD Thursday our procurement team can start the temporary attestation review.

Sara
Sara Lim
Security & Compliance Lead | Hearthline Analytics
sara.lim@hearthline.com

Sara — quick ops note from our side:

- We can provision an SFTP home for the evidence handoff and also support a temporary pre-signed object store link if that9s easier for your team. Dylan will coordinate the upload format and a short manifest (filenames + descriptions).
- For the OneTrust flow: if you add lauren_bishop@redwood.com and dylan_brooks@redwood.com to the form invite we9ll triage the DDQ and fill in technical detail sections.
- Bridge letter: I9ve reviewed the attached draft and we9ll send an updated, redwood-signed PDF after Aditya confirms a couple of legal points.

Thanks — we9ll aim to have the bridge letter + SFTP details to you within 3 business days.

Lauren Bishop
Security Ops | Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com
